title: Noise estimator benchmark: find_noise_level vs noise_san_plot
question: Should the isolated-peak bug be fixed by switching the noise estimator to noise_san_plot instead of repairing find_noise_level?
verdict: No. Keep find_noise_level. SanPlot gives identical recall (968/970) but returns about 1.85x more peaks (junk). The right fix is to repair the single-segment branch in find_noise_level, which recovers the isolated peaks without SanPlot's extra peaks.
how_it_was_run: One process ran find_peaks twice on every EIC, once with NoiseMethod::FindNoiseLevel and once with NoiseMethod::SanPlot, on the exact same real data. Only the noise method differs. Code in core/examples/noise_bench.rs.

settings.note: Same detection settings as the real TripleTOF get_features run (scripts/run_gf_full.R).

isolated_cases.note: rt 35.89 is past the 35 min window cutoff for both arms; not a noise-method effect

why_sanplot_underperforms: SanPlot assumes noise is symmetric around a center. Our EIC is baseline-subtracted and clamped at zero, so the lower half of that shape is gone. On a sparse window SanPlot reports a near-zero noise floor, so it finds weak isolated peaks but also lets real noise through everywhere else, which is the extra 48191 peaks.
caveats: This is the find_peaks level (targeted EIC per truth feature). The noise method acts only here, so the full get_features numbers move with it. peaks_returned is the junk proxy: same EICs, more peaks = more false detections.

TripleTOF has only 3 isolated-peak cases, so this run mainly measures the downside (junk). The upside (recovering the 27 QE HF isolated-peak cases) is delivered by the find_noise_level single-segment fix, not by SanPlot.
TTOF0459 is missed by both because its rt 35.89 is outside the 0.4-35 min window; it is a window artifact, not a noise-method result.
